papers.title: AMP-GSM: Prediction of Antimicrobial Peptides via a Grouping–Scoring–Modeling Approach
Interpretable support vector classifier for reliable prediction of antibacterial activity of modified peptides against Escherichia coli.

models.architecture_or_algorithm: Grouping–Scoring–Modeling approach with feature selection and classifier (unspecified classifier)
models.input_features: physicochemical, linguistic, sequence, and structure-based features grouped into sub-datasets
models.candidate_reason: Provides performance comparison (AUC 99% Gram-negative, 98% Gram-positive) and uses feature grouping; could be benchmarked if code/data become available.
models.representative_reason: Feature grouping approach for Gram-positive/negative classification, could represent traditional ML with physicochemical features

models.task_type: AMP prediction / anti-E. coli activity classification
models.architecture_or_algorithm: Support vector machine (SVM) with SHAP explainability, using ECFP fingerprints and carbon-carbon pair fraction
models.input_features: SMILES strings (converted to ECFP fingerprints and fraction of carbon-carbon pairs)
models.candidate_reason: Reports AUROC 91.83% and MCC 71.86%, outperforms AntiMPmod; model is interpretable. Could be benchmarked if code/data available.
models.representative_reason: SVM-based interpretable model for anti-E. coli activity prediction using SMILES, could represent structure-based AMP classification
